matches.rationale: The ground truth is a paper-wide computational error in which galaxies are treated as being in a different reference frame from the observer, producing flawed equations. Pred 6 attacks the eq. (3) derivation that manufactures the claim that galaxies (at fixed position) acquire a distinct four-velocity/frame; pred 4 pinpoints the unrecorded frame switch in d\Omega_O between eqs. (26) and (28) that generates the modified angular distance; pred 1 shows the resulting distances violate the Etherington relation, i.e. the invalid downstream results. Together these name the same frame-mixing defect in the computations.

pred_verdicts.rationale: Demonstrates that the frame-corrected distances yield an invalid Etherington relation, the flawed-result consequence of the ground-truth frame assumption.
Correctly notes a missing /5 in the distance-modulus inversion, a transcription typo not in the ground truth.
Correct observation about the misprinted Doppler relation (z vs 1+z), an independent typo.
Identifies the unmarked change of reference frame in d\Omega_O between eqs. (26) and (28) that underlies the modified angular distance.
Flags a transcription slip (1+z'^2 vs (1+z')^2) in the H definition, unrelated to the ground-truth frame error.
Refutes the eq. (3) manipulation that is used to assert galaxies occupy a distinct (moving) frame, the root of the ground-truth defect.
Raises a distinct, correct issue about solid-angle conservation in the CMB multipole argument rather than the frame-assumption defect.
Points out a mistyped definition of I_G, a minor pre-existing notational slip.
